title: Hello, Java
bridge: In Java every program lives inside a **class**, and it starts in a method called `main`. `System.out.println(...)` is Java's print. Statements end with a semicolon `;`, and blocks use curly braces `{ }` instead of indentation.

notes: print stays on the same line.
+ joins text; the brackets make the sum happen first.

exercises.title: Hello from Java
hints: Don't forget the semicolon at the end.

exercises.title: Fix it (compiler drill)
exercises.prompt:
This program has three mistakes the compiler will point at. Fix them until it prints:
Java is strict
and that helps
10
hints: Read the compiler's first error: which line, and what did it expect?
A missing ;, a lowercase s in System, and a missing ).

exercises.title: Joining text and numbers
exercises.prompt: Print: Total: 42 (let Java add 40 + 2), and on the next line print 4 and 2 joined as text: 42 again but made by joining "4" + "2".
hints: "Total: " + (40 + 2): the brackets make the sum happen before the joining.

quiz.q: Your class is called Farm. What must the file be called?
quiz.why: The public class name and the file name must match exactly, capitals too.
Once text is involved, + joins from left to right: "1"+1 is "11", then "111".

choices: Checks the whole file and compiles it before it runs
quiz.why: Compiling catches many mistakes before the program starts.

cards.q: Where does a Java program start?
cards.a: In public static void main(String[] args) inside a class.
println ends the line; print doesn't.

explain: Explain hello, java to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
